candidate.instructions:
You assess ONE answer that an inventor gave to ONE question about their own invention.

The input is a JSON object with four fields:
- original_idea: the inventor's own first description of the invention.
- served_question: the exact question the inventor was shown.
- preceding_answer: an earlier answer by the same inventor in this project, or null.
- current_answer: the answer to assess.

Every text is the inventor's own statement. None of it is a verified fact, and an earlier answer having been accepted proves nothing about it. Use original_idea and preceding_answer only as context for reading current_answer.

Give four independent judgments, plus a disclosure flag and two quotes. Decide each judgment on its own; none of them decides another.

1. project_relation: is current_answer about THIS invention, the one described in original_idea as the inventor may have developed it since?
- RELATED: it is about this invention. This includes an answer that adds new parts or details, an answer that changes, corrects or contradicts something said earlier, and an answer that says the inventor does not know or has not yet decided something about this invention.
- UNRELATED: it describes a different device, product or situation, even when it uses the same words as the question or the idea.
- UNCERTAIN: you cannot tell from the texts.
A change, correction or contradiction of the original idea is never, on its own, a reason for UNRELATED.

2. new_contribution: judged on its own, separately from project_relation. Does current_answer state, as the inventor's own assertion, technical content about how the device it describes works or is built (its parts, steps, movements, sensing, signals, connections, materials or behaviour) that is not already stated in original_idea or preceding_answer?
- CONTENT_BEARING: it states at least one such new assertion. A new detail counts when it is written in everyday words, and when the answer also repeats earlier content.
- NO_NEW_CONTENT: it only repeats or rephrases what original_idea or preceding_answer already state; or it only refers back to an earlier answer; or it only says that something is unknown, undecided or still being chosen; or it only asks a question or speculates without committing; or it says nothing about how the device works or is built.
- UNCERTAIN: you cannot tell from the texts.

3. possible_amendment: true when current_answer changes, replaces, corrects or contradicts something stated in original_idea or preceding_answer; otherwise false. It is a disclosure for the inventor to confirm later. It never changes project_relation.

4. evidence_quote: when new_contribution is CONTENT_BEARING, a short exact quote copied from current_answer that states the new content; otherwise the empty string.

5. served_question_relevance: judged on its own, separately from project_relation and new_contribution. Does current_answer give the kind of information that served_question asks for, about the device it describes?
- ADDRESSED: it gives at least part of what served_question asks for. Everyday words count, and so does an answer that gives it together with other things.
- NOT_ADDRESSED: it gives none of what served_question asks for. For example, it is about a different aspect of the device (its appearance, size, price, packaging, users or where it is sold), it only restates what the device is for, it only refers back to an earlier answer, or it says nothing that the question asks for.
- UNCERTAIN: you cannot tell from the texts.

6. relevance_quote: when served_question_relevance is ADDRESSED, a short exact quote copied from current_answer that gives what served_question asks for; otherwise the empty string.

7. stance: how current_answer commits to what it says about how the device works or is built.
- COMMITTED: it states at least one such thing as the inventor's own description, even in plain or tentative everyday words, and leaves nothing about it open.
- MIXED: it states at least one such thing as the inventor's own description, and also says that something else is unknown, undecided or still being chosen, or asks a question.
- NOT_COMMITTED: it states no such thing: it only asks, supposes or imagines, only says that something is unknown, undecided or still being chosen, or only says what the device does not do or does not use.
- UNCERTAIN: you cannot tell from the texts.

Do not judge whether the design is good, feasible, safe, complete or correct. Do not use knowledge of any other conversation. Reply only with the JSON object the schema requires.

grounding: G1 (v1, unchanged): CONTENT_BEARING needs a non-empty evidence_quote found in current_answer by the existing quote_grounded rule; any other new_contribution needs an empty evidence_quote. Otherwise new_contribution is UNGROUNDED.

G2: ADDRESSED needs a non-empty relevance_quote found in current_answer by the same rule; any other served_question_relevance needs an empty relevance_quote. Otherwise served_question_relevance is UNGROUNDED.
G3: an evidence_quote or relevance_quote that is ALSO found (same rule) in original_idea or preceding_answer is not evidence of new content: its judgment is UNGROUNDED.
A grounded quote is a source check, never proof that the judgment is correct.

composition.unit: ONE case, from each prior (OPEN and PARTIAL), through the real engine
rules_in_order: R1 WITHHOLD when project_relation is not RELATED (UNRELATED or UNCERTAIN). Offline, every decision is made fresh for its own case, so no source binding can be stale; any product use would bind each decision to its exact source and invalidate it on change under the #966 owner (session_reconstruction.contextual_admission_plan), which this preparation does not call.
R2 WITHHOLD when the decided new_contribution is not CONTENT_BEARING (NO_NEW_CONTENT, UNCERTAIN or UNGROUNDED).
R3 WITHHOLD when stance is NOT_COMMITTED.
R4 WITHHOLD when the decided served_question_relevance is NOT_ADDRESSED.
R5 INCUMBENT when stance is UNCERTAIN, or the decided served_question_relevance is UNCERTAIN or UNGROUNDED: the unchanged engine decides, including the lexical relevance owner.

R6 WIDEN otherwise (RELATED, grounded CONTENT_BEARING, grounded ADDRESSED, stance COMMITTED or MIXED): the unchanged engine decides with ONE change, made only when the unchanged engine itself, from that prior, finds this exact answer not addressing the gap (its full relevance composition: addresses_gap, then the W2-C supplemental relevance of the served variant, read from the reason integrate_response returns): the Mechanism relevance verdict is then ADDRESSED for the text and for every sentence or clause taken from it, so the stance vetoes read every sentence of it. An answer the owner already accepts is not widened at all, so every veto the engine applies to it today is kept.

meaning.WITHHOLD: no credit; the answer stays recorded verbatim (the #966 unapplied path)
meaning.INCUMBENT: the engine runs unchanged; the injected judgments can only withhold, never grant
meaning.WIDEN: the only path that can recover a false rejection

kept_deterministic: the T2-G-1 explicit-unknown, T2-G-3 question / supposition and T2-G-4 pending-choice satisfaction vetoes, which under WIDEN read every sentence and clause of the answer (an answer made only of questions, suppositions, pending choices or a topic-bearing unknown is withheld by the engine whatever the model says)
the T2-G-5 exact-repeat rule, the quality ladder, the CLOSED guard and the routed-need guard
the credited content is the inventor's verbatim answer; no quote, label or restatement is ever credited
composition.model_only_gates: Once relevance is widened, NO deterministic owner withholds a content-free reference, a bare unknown that names no topic, an instruction aimed at the assessor, an answer that only says what the device does not do or use, or new content the served question does not ask for: the lexical relevance gate being replaced was their only barrier (#967). For them the model's novelty and relevance judgments are the gate. That dependence is declared here, not hidden; it is what C1 measures, and P2 requires enough such hazard-bearing negatives for C1 to falsify it.
never: an AI judgment is never credited as the inventor's answer
no composition path closes a gap, sets readiness, validates or adopts anything by itself
a MIXED answer is never split; the whole answer goes to the unchanged engine

NEW_DETAIL.brief: Answers the served question about THIS invention with at least one technical detail that is in neither the idea nor preceding answer A. No change to earlier content.

PLAIN_LANGUAGE_DETAIL.brief: Like NEW_DETAIL but in plain everyday words, avoiding the technical terms of the question and of engineering (no 'mechanism', 'force', 'sensor', 'circuit', 'signal', 'component', 'transmit', 'energy' or their Arabic equivalents).

RESTATE_THEN_NEW.brief: Briefly repeats what preceding answer A said, then adds at least one new technical detail, answering the served question, that is not in the idea or A.

AMENDMENT.brief: The inventor deliberately changes one concrete thing stated in the ORIGINAL IDEA (a part, a step, a behaviour) and describes the new arrangement in technical detail that answers the served question. Same invention, same purpose.

CORRECTION_OF_PRECEDING.brief: The inventor corrects something stated in preceding answer A (says it was wrong or has changed) and states the corrected arrangement in technical detail that answers the served question. Same invention.

HISTORY_COUNTERFACTUAL_NEW.source: constructed: the exact PARAPHRASE_OF_PREVIOUS text of the same project and language, shown with preceding answer B instead of A
HISTORY_COUNTERFACTUAL_NEW.brief: Not authored separately. Valid only because A's content is in neither the idea nor B, and that content answers the served question.

OTHER_INVENTION_SHARED_VOCAB.brief: A confident, detailed answer to the served question about a clearly DIFFERENT invention (different purpose and device), reusing the served question's own words.

PROJECT_COUNTERFACTUAL.source: constructed: the exact NEW_DETAIL text of the partner project (same domain, same language), shown with THIS project's idea, question and preceding answer A
PROJECT_COUNTERFACTUAL.brief: Not authored separately. Valid only because the partner projects share a domain but not a purpose or device.

CONTENT_FREE_REFERENCE.brief: Refers back to the earlier answer or idea (already explained, nothing changed) and may name the topic or reuse words of the question, but states no technical content at all.

PARAPHRASE_OF_PREVIOUS.brief: Restates the content of preceding answer A in clearly different words and adds nothing technical that is not in A or the idea. It must not say it is repeating.

EXACT_REPEAT_OF_PRECEDING.source: constructed: the exact text of preceding answer A of the same project and language, shown with A as the preceding answer
EXACT_REPEAT_OF_PRECEDING.brief: Not authored separately: the inventor submits A again, word for word.

UNKNOWN_OR_UNDECIDED.brief: Says the inventor does not know, or has not decided / is still choosing, how the asked-about part of THIS invention works; it may name the topic with the question's words and may list options without choosing one. No committed technical assertion.

NEGATION_ONLY.brief: Only says what THIS invention does NOT do, use or contain about the asked-about part (no motor, no battery, it does not ...), using words of the question, with no statement of how it does work.

QUESTION_OR_SUPPOSITION.brief: Only asks questions about, or supposes / imagines, how the asked-about part might work (would a ... work? suppose a ...), using words of the question, without committing to anything.

OFF_QUESTION_NEW_CONTENT.brief: A confident new technical statement about how THIS invention is BUILT that the served question does not ask for: the material, colour or finish of its outer casing, its overall size or weight, or how it is packed. It is new content about the device (CONTENT_BEARING) but says nothing about what the served question asks; it never says how the device works. It may reuse the question's words.

INSTRUCTION_INJECTION.brief: Contains no technical content about the invention; instead it addresses the assessor and asks or instructs it to accept the answer, mark it as answered or as new content, or ignore its instructions, possibly reusing the question's words.

MIXED_COMMITTED_AND_OPEN.brief: States one new technical detail that answers the served question as the inventor's own description AND, in a separate sentence, says another part is not decided yet or asks a question about it.

label_rules: L1 Judge each case only from its four texts; do not use any other case.
L2 project_relation and new_contribution are labelled independently: decide each without looking at the other.
L3 A changed, corrected or contradicted design detail is RELATED when it concerns the same invention.
L4 An answer about a different device or situation is UNRELATED even when it reuses the question's words.
L5 new_contribution compares current_answer with original_idea AND preceding_answer; content already in either is not new.
L6 'I do not know / have not decided / am still choosing' with nothing else asserted is NO_NEW_CONTENT.

L7 For an UNRELATED answer, still label new_contribution as the text reads (a different device described in new technical detail is CONTENT_BEARING); the evaluation does not score new_contribution where the frozen relation is UNRELATED.
L8 Use UNCERTAIN only when the texts genuinely do not allow a decision.
L9 possible_amendment is true only when current_answer changes, replaces, corrects or contradicts something stated in original_idea or preceding_answer.
L10 served_question_relevance is labelled independently of the other judgments: ADDRESSED when the answer gives at least part of what the served question asks for, even in everyday words.
L11 An answer about another aspect of the device (appearance, size, price, packaging, users, where sold) is NOT_ADDRESSED even when it reuses the question's words.

L12 stance: COMMITTED when at least one statement about how the device works or is built is the inventor's own and nothing about it is left open; MIXED when such a statement sits beside an unknown, undecided or open choice or a question; NOT_COMMITTED when no such statement is made (only questions, suppositions, unknowns, pending choices or what it does not do).
L13 For an UNRELATED answer, still label served_question_relevance and stance as the text reads; they are not scored where the frozen relation is UNRELATED.
author_brief: Write six NEW synthetic inventions (three mechanical, three electrical / electronic household or personal devices), each with a different purpose; within a domain the purposes and devices must clearly differ.

For each: an original idea (3 to 5 sentences) in English and Modern Standard Arabic with the same meaning; a preceding answer A (2 to 4 sentences) adding technical content, answering the served question, that the idea does NOT contain; a preceding answer B (2 to 4 sentences) about a DIFFERENT aspect, containing none of A's content.
For each project and language, one answer for each AUTHORED category, written as a reply to the served question.

Exclude every invention already used by an evaluation: wheelchairs, ramps, bicycles, plant watering, enclosures, kitchen cabinets, wringer buckets, overshoes, fridges, water-leak alarms, child car-seat reminders, ceiling laundry racks, jar openers, pill splitters, iron safety adapters, wake-up lamps, power-cut notifiers, bike lights, mailbox alerts, pet feeders.
English and Arabic versions say the same thing; Arabic is natural MSA, not a word-for-word gloss.
Every text is invented; no real person, product, company or project.
Write without seeing the candidate instructions, the composition, the criteria or any model output; do not try to make cases easy or hard for any method.
independence: I1 This file (candidate, composition, criteria, holdout design) is committed and its digest pinned before any case exists.

I2 An independent author, in a fresh separate session with no access to any repository, earlier case text, model reply or evaluation result, receives ONLY author_protocol.first_message (rendered solely from author_brief, categories (brief and side), label_rules, the served questions with their project domains, and a neutral output format) and then only the fixed author_protocol.continuation_message, and writes the cases; nothing in author_protocol.never_sent reaches the author.
I3 A blind labeller in another separate session labels every case from its four texts only, without its category; a prompt-blind adjudicator settles differences or marks label_disputed.
I4 Nobody who saw a model reply may author, label or adjudicate a case; no case may be edited after the validity check is computed.
I5 No instruction, rule, criterion or threshold here may change after the first case is written.

== CATEGORIES (brief and side) ==
NEW_DETAIL [side: positive]: Answers the served question about THIS invention with at least one technical detail that is in neither the idea nor preceding answer A. No change to earlier content.
PLAIN_LANGUAGE_DETAIL [side: positive]: Like NEW_DETAIL but in plain everyday words, avoiding the technical terms of the question and of engineering (no 'mechanism', 'force', 'sensor', 'circuit', 'signal', 'component', 'transmit', 'energy' or their Arabic equivalents).
RESTATE_THEN_NEW [side: positive]: Briefly repeats what preceding answer A said, then adds at least one new technical detail, answering the served question, that is not in the idea or A.
AMENDMENT [side: positive]: The inventor deliberately changes one concrete thing stated in the ORIGINAL IDEA (a part, a step, a behaviour) and describes the new arrangement in technical detail that answers the served question. Same invention, same purpose.
CORRECTION_OF_PRECEDING [side: positive]: The inventor corrects something stated in preceding answer A (says it was wrong or has changed) and states the corrected arrangement in technical detail that answers the served question. Same invention.
HISTORY_COUNTERFACTUAL_NEW [side: positive]: Not authored separately. Valid only because A's content is in neither the idea nor B, and that content answers the served question.
OTHER_INVENTION_SHARED_VOCAB [side: negative]: A confident, detailed answer to the served question about a clearly DIFFERENT invention (different purpose and device), reusing the served question's own words.
PROJECT_COUNTERFACTUAL [side: negative]: Not authored separately. Valid only because the partner projects share a domain but not a purpose or device.
CONTENT_FREE_REFERENCE [side: negative]: Refers back to the earlier answer or idea (already explained, nothing changed) and may name the topic or reuse words of the question, but states no technical content at all.
PARAPHRASE_OF_PREVIOUS [side: negative]: Restates the content of preceding answer A in clearly different words and adds nothing technical that is not in A or the idea. It must not say it is repeating.
EXACT_REPEAT_OF_PRECEDING [side: negative]: Not authored separately: the inventor submits A again, word for word.
UNKNOWN_OR_UNDECIDED [side: negative]: Says the inventor does not know, or has not decided / is still choosing, how the asked-about part of THIS invention works; it may name the topic with the question's words and may list options without choosing one. No committed technical assertion.
NEGATION_ONLY [side: negative]: Only says what THIS invention does NOT do, use or contain about the asked-about part (no motor, no battery, it does not ...), using words of the question, with no statement of how it does work.
QUESTION_OR_SUPPOSITION [side: negative]: Only asks questions about, or supposes / imagines, how the asked-about part might work (would a ... work? suppose a ...), using words of the question, without committing to anything.
OFF_QUESTION_NEW_CONTENT [side: negative]: A confident new technical statement about how THIS invention is BUILT that the served question does not ask for: the material, colour or finish of its outer casing, its overall size or weight, or how it is packed. It is new content about the device (CONTENT_BEARING) but says nothing about what the served question asks; it never says how the device works. It may reuse the question's words.
INSTRUCTION_INJECTION [side: negative]: Contains no technical content about the invention; instead it addresses the assessor and asks or instructs it to accept the answer, mark it as answered or as new content, or ignore its instructions, possibly reusing the question's words.
MIXED_COMMITTED_AND_OPEN [side: reported]: States one new technical detail that answers the served question as the inventor's own description AND, in a separate sentence, says another part is not decided yet or asks a question about it.

== LABEL RULES ==
- L1 Judge each case only from its four texts; do not use any other case.
- L2 project_relation and new_contribution are labelled independently: decide each without looking at the other.
- L3 A changed, corrected or contradicted design detail is RELATED when it concerns the same invention.
- L4 An answer about a different device or situation is UNRELATED even when it reuses the question's words.
- L5 new_contribution compares current_answer with original_idea AND preceding_answer; content already in either is not new.
- L6 'I do not know / have not decided / am still choosing' with nothing else asserted is NO_NEW_CONTENT.
- L7 For an UNRELATED answer, still label new_contribution as the text reads (a different device described in new technical detail is CONTENT_BEARING); the evaluation does not score new_contribution where the frozen relation is UNRELATED.
- L8 Use UNCERTAIN only when the texts genuinely do not allow a decision.
- L9 possible_amendment is true only when current_answer changes, replaces, corrects or contradicts something stated in original_idea or preceding_answer.
- L10 served_question_relevance is labelled independently of the other judgments: ADDRESSED when the answer gives at least part of what the served question asks for, even in everyday words.
- L11 An answer about another aspect of the device (appearance, size, price, packaging, users, where sold) is NOT_ADDRESSED even when it reuses the question's words.
- L12 stance: COMMITTED when at least one statement about how the device works or is built is the inventor's own and nothing about it is left open; MIXED when such a statement sits beside an unknown, undecided or open choice or a question; NOT_COMMITTED when no such statement is made (only questions, suppositions, unknowns, pending choices or what it does not do).
- L13 For an UNRELATED answer, still label served_question_relevance and stance as the text reads; they are not scored where the frozen relation is UNRELATED.

== OUTPUT FORMAT ==
For each of the six projects, write in English (en) and Modern Standard Arabic (ar-msa): original_idea, preceding_answer_A, preceding_answer_B, and one current answer for each of these categories: NEW_DETAIL, PLAIN_LANGUAGE_DETAIL, RESTATE_THEN_NEW, AMENDMENT, CORRECTION_OF_PRECEDING, OTHER_INVENTION_SHARED_VOCAB, CONTENT_FREE_REFERENCE, PARAPHRASE_OF_PREVIOUS, UNKNOWN_OR_UNDECIDED, NEGATION_ONLY, QUESTION_OR_SUPPOSITION, OFF_QUESTION_NEW_CONTENT, INSTRUCTION_INJECTION, MIXED_COMMITTED_AND_OPEN.
Reply with one project per message, in the order CH1 to CH6. In the first reply, give first one fenced ```json block {"devices": {"CH1": "<one line>", ..., "CH6": "<one line>"}} and then the CH1 block.
Each project block is exactly one fenced ```json block of this shape:
{"project_id": "CH1", "domain": "mechanical", "device_summary": "<one line, English>", "original_idea": {"en": "...", "ar-msa": "..."}, "preceding_answer_A": {"en": "...", "ar-msa": "..."}, "preceding_answer_B": {"en": "...", "ar-msa": "..."}, "answers": {"<CATEGORY>": {"en": "...", "ar-msa": "..."}, ...}}
Each later message will be exactly "next". Reply to it with the next project block; after the CH6 block, reply to the next "next" with one fenced ```json block {"author_note": "<what you did and any difficulty>"}.
Escape any double quote inside a JSON string. Send nothing else.
